doc.text: Bottle Hydro Dates and cascade pressures

Michael Hutt, H2S daily, XTO "BAGGEYT gu1h", 10:08 AM — both fields entered as the single character "N": "N Pressure on Cascade System N Bottle Hydro Dates". Neither a pressure nor a date. This is a repeat — Hutt has been entering Bottle Hydro Dates as "N" on prior days. His form carries a full set of air-trailer photos, so a trailer was on location; the board does not list this job, so I could not confirm an AT# against it.

1099 Benjamin Boutte, H2S daily, SM Energy Junior Mint flowback, 09:13 AM — Pressure on Cascade System reads "1900"; Bottle Hydro Dates is blank. Board AT# for that assignment is 127, so a trailer is named and the blank is a valid finding. This is also a repeat, though an improvement on prior days: the cascade pressure is now filled and only the hydro date is missing.

1099 Hayden Haugh, H2S daily, Ovintiv H&P 616 — both fields read "N/a". His assignment is on neither board sheet so no AT# could be confirmed, and six of his air-trailer photo fields carry no capture at all. Needs confirmation whether a trailer was on that location before this is called a finding.

Clean on these fields: Dennis Easley ("4@2200 psi" / "4@3/23") and Allen White ("4@2300" / "4@3-23"), both complete. On the Readiness Forms, every cascade entry from Ralph Forbes (605), Andrew Bailey (602), Larry Jaramillo (606), Nathan Contreras (503), 1099 Rolando Flores (600), Pablo Soto (604) and 1099 Robert Henigan (175) carries both a pressure and a hydro date on the charged bottles, with "N/A", "Na" or "O" on the empty positions — all complete, none a finding.

Exempt because AT# is N/A: the Comstock drilling EIR inspection route (Larry Taylor) and both Southwest Operating standby rows on the ETX sheet. No trailer equipment fields or trailer forms are required for those.
Photos not taken on the day being verified

Michael Hutt, rig check, Crimson Tide 1H — eighteen photos all stamped 07/15/2025 07:38 AM, covering the condition sign, monitor placement and source, repeater, loud alarm placement and source, windsock, muster point, SCBA checklist, pressure gauge and mask, ELSA placement and gauge, sensor placement, radio address, battery power, calibration date and skid date. Only the monitor display picture and the JSA upload are from 10/10. The repeater faceplate and the checklist upload have no image at all. Effectively the whole rig check is evidenced by a fifteen-month-old photo set.

Comments to management other than N/A

None. Every "Comments or Concerns for Management" field on 10/10 reads "N/A" or is blank. The only substantive management comment of the day is Robert Henigan's empty-tank report, which sits in the Readiness Form's equivalent field and is covered above.

Seven of the eight Trailer Readiness Forms left "Is anything wrong or missing? If so what and who was notified?" entirely blank — Forbes, Bailey, Jaramillo, Contreras, Flores, Soto and Marquez-Salazar. Blank is a legitimate answer when nothing is wrong, but it is worth confirming the field is being read rather than skipped, given it is the only place a trailer problem gets recorded.

clean.text: Larry Taylor filed a complete field service form for TGNR at J14E Hull Pad with the work described and every photo taken on the day. Brey Rasco's Mitsui Lipsey 1H supervision form is properly paused and ended across the two days with the ticket detail recorded. 1099 Cindy Smith's two air jobs were the best-documented of the day — full multi-selects, complete Learn sections, on-date photos throughout, and a clear narrative of the benzene she detected. Nathan Contreras filed seven forms — four Trailer Inspection Forms, a Readiness Form, two air jobs and a field service job — all with FR answered Yes, comments N/A, on-date photos and completed narratives, with only the AV-3000 question on his Readiness Form left open. 1099 Rolando Flores, 1099 Justin Fontenot and 1099 William Jimmy Cooper all filed full OWL reviews with substantive narratives.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images, not as text — which matters today in particular for Michael Hutt, whose fire extinguisher tag photo on the H2S daily is fifteen months old, so tag currency cannot be verified from that submission at all.

64 of 64 submissions read. The job board was available but not current: Blake Walton's most recent board email is dated 10/8/2026 and no board was sent on 10/9 or 10/10. The ArkLaTex workbook from that email contains a "10-10 DRAFT" sheet, which was used for ETX; the Permian Basin workbook's latest sheet is "10-9 DRAFT", which was used for WTX as the closest available. Twelve manned board rows carrying a named technician were checked for coverage — 5 on the ETX 10-10 sheet and 7 on the WTX 10-9 sheet. Roughly forty XTO AGT rows on the WTX sheet carry a location but no technician and no AT# and could not be checked, and several jobs that were actually worked on 10/10 — the XTO Baggett GU #1 supervision, the Crimson Tide 1H rig check, both SM Energy rig downs, the TGNR field service and the Ovintiv H&P 616 supervision — appear on neither sheet.
